title: Sednit_Backdoor_Investigation_829
description: Investigate a compromised host exhibiting signs of Sednit backdoor activity.
outcomes: Learn to identify suspicious services using systemd service management
Learn to determine persistence mechanisms using systemd timers
Learn to identify suspicious processes using process monitoring tools

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Sednit group is known for using sophisticated malware to compromise networks. In this scenario, you will investigate a compromised host that exhibits signs of Sednit backdoor activity. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the host and perform necessary actions to contain and eradicate the threat. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the host and perform necessary actions to contain and eradicate the threat. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the `target` host and identify the suspicious service running on the system.
levels.solution: Run `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and look for the suspicious service named `scroll.dll`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by listing all services running on the system.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service has an unusual name.

hints.title: Fourth hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to find the service.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine the timer responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service.
levels.solution: Run `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers and look for the timer named `local-inventory`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by listing all timers running on the system.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that seem out of place or have unusual configurations.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The timer responsible for the persistence has an unusual name.

hints.title: Fourth hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to find the timer.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Process
levels.content: Identify the process responsible for suspicious activity on the host.
levels.solution: Run `ps aux` to list all processes and look for the process named `ncat`.

hints.title: First hint title

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for processes that seem out of place or have unusual configurations.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The process responsible for the suspicious activity has an unusual name.

hints.title: Fourth hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ps aux` to find the process.
